page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.se1ne.6xlarge is a memory-optimized virtual server instance belonging to the ecs.se1ne family, running on the KVM hypervisor. It features 24 dedicated physical cores and 24 vCPUs powered by an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor operating at a base frequency of 2.5 GHz. The instance is equipped with 192.0 GB of RAM, providing a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, and it offers a baseline network bandwidth of 4 Gbps.

Benchmark data indicates a clear distinction between single-core and multi-core performance. Single-core metrics, such as the stress-ng single-core CPU test and Geekbench single-core score, fall into the weak category, which is also reflected in the poor single-threaded gzip compression throughput. However, the instance leverages its 24 dedicated cores to deliver average multi-core performance, as demonstrated by the stress-ng multi-core and Geekbench multi-core benchmarks. Memory bandwidth tests for both small cached and large uncached blocks consistently register in the average tier, supporting steady data throughput.

The primary tradeoff of the ecs.se1ne.6xlarge is its modest single-threaded processing speed, making it less suitable for latency-sensitive, single-core bound applications. From a cost-efficiency perspective, the instance provides a dense memory profile relative to its compute resources, offering a balanced option for memory-intensive workloads that do not require high-frequency single-core performance. It is well-suited for database operations, multi-threaded text and image processing, static web serving, and moderate-scale Redis deployments.
